lower_bound.quote: there is a set $V_T\subseteq\{0,\dots,n\}$ and signs $s:V_T\to\{\pm1\}$ such that the signed sum $\Xi:=\sum_{j\in V_T}s(j)\,q_j$ satisfies $|\Xi|\le\sum_i\varepsilon_i+[M\text{ odd}]\,a_M$ (standard; details omitted).
lower_bound.witness: Missing statement: for every refinement A of the geometric pieces (2^n u,...,u) by at most n cuts, with the consecutive pairs P_i of the sorted parts viewed as edges on the original pieces, one must construct (for all n and all refinements) a nonempty vertex set V_T and signs s such that |sum_{j in V_T} s(j) q_j| <= sum_i eps_i + [M odd] a_M. This is the entire content of Lemma 4 (the only nontrivial step connecting the pairing slack to the signed subset-sum property (3.1)); the text merely names a 'tree-component argument' and explicitly omits the details. Numerical checks (brute force n<=4, Monte Carlo) do not substitute for the argument.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The lower-bound conclusion D(A) >= u, hence Liu Bang's guarantee of (1+u)/2 = c, rests entirely on Lemma 4, whose only substantive inequality is the omitted one.

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) stated. Lemma 2 (greedy value = odd-rank sum) and Lemma 5 (subset-sum pigeonhole + cross-pairing cuts) are fully argued and check out. Lemma 4's key inequality is asserted as 'standard; details omitted', so the lower bound is not written.
